plan.title: Upgrade workflow should carry framework updates through default-branch release handoff

narratives.Description: A consumer framework upgrade can refresh the deposit and even land a framework-only commit while still leaving the default branch without the update. This story closes that gap by defining end-to-end SCM release handoff after a successful deposit, with named terminal states released, pr-open, or blocked, and policy-aware PR vs direct-commit paths that honor the human merge gate.
narratives.Overview:
## Problem

A consumer framework upgrade can successfully refresh the deposit (and even land a framework-only commit) while still leaving the operator goal incomplete: **the released default branch does not yet carry the framework update.**

Installer/update success ≠ upgrade released. From the operator's perspective, `update directive` / sync is unfinished until one of these terminal states is true:

- **released** — default branch carries the framework update;
- **pr-open** — framework-only branch pushed and PR opened, awaiting review/merge per policy;
- **blocked** — explicit reason (branch protection, dirty tree, auth, human-merge gate, CI, etc.).

## Observed behavior (historical + still-true class)

Historical repro (2026-06-12, `statusreport`, vendored payload `v0.45.1` → `v0.46.0`, Go installer path):

- Update machinery refreshed `.deft/core` / managed files and produced a framework-only deposit.
- Agent created `chore/deft-update-v0.46.0` and committed.
- Skill/workflow exited after the local commit — no push, no PR, no merge, no terminal operator state.

That class still holds on the **current canonical path** (`npm i -g @deftai/directive@latest` + `directive update` / `deft update`): deposit and managed-file refresh can complete without a defined SCM release handoff. `deft-directive-sync` still ends at "Shall I commit …?" without push/PR/merge/terminal release states, and still leads with submodule phases while npm is only a banner.

## Expected behavior

Upgrade guidance (skill + docs + recovery prose) must define an **end-to-end handoff** after a successful deposit:

1. Detect consumer branch policy (`plan.policy.allowDirectCommitsToMaster`, branch protection / `requireHumanMerge`).
2. **Branch-protected / human-merge** repos: offer (or perform with consent) push of a framework-only branch + open PR; stop at **pr-open** unless policy allows bot merge.
3. **Direct-commit-enabled** repos: explicit default-branch path with confirmation; end at **released**.
4. Always emit a single terminal state: `released` | `pr-open` | `blocked:<reason>`.
5. Do **not** auto-merge past `requireHumanMerge` / human merge gate (#1193).

## Current canonical upgrade path (do not reinvent)

Hot path today (#761 / #2274 / #1409 / #2064):

```bash
npm i -g @deftai/directive@latest   # or pnpm equivalent
directive update                    # or: deft update
directive doctor                    # confirm deposit health
```

Legacy Go `deft-install --yes --upgrade --repo-root . --json` remains a **no-Node / offline bridge only**, not the primary AC surface.

This issue is **not** "make update deposit the payload" — that works. It is **carry a successful deposit through consumer SCM release handoff**.

## Scope

### In scope

- Terminal operator states after successful framework deposit (skill + docs).
- Policy-aware branch vs default-branch paths.
- Explicit next-step naming when the workflow stops short of default branch (never silent stop after local commit only).
- Align `deft-directive-sync` (and any upgrade-handoff guidance) so npm+`directive update` is the primary path; submodule flow is legacy/back-compat only.
- Framework-only change set discipline (do not mix product feature work into the upgrade commit/PR).

### Out of scope

- Replacing npm as the canonical install/upgrade transport.
- Auto-merge when `requireHumanMerge` is true.
- Full review-cycle ownership for product PRs (use existing review-cycle skill when a PR is opened).
- Dirty-worktree transactional checkpoints (#2849) except as a **blocked** reason if needed.
- Build-skill story handoff (#1598) except cross-link for shared "finish in an explicit handoff state" pattern.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After a successful deposit, upgrade guidance never ends at "local framework-only commit" without naming the next release step.
- [ ] Workflow records one terminal state: `released` | `pr-open` | `blocked:<reason>`.
- [ ] Branch-protected / human-merge consumers get a PR-oriented path; direct-commit-enabled consumers get an explicit default-branch path.
- [ ] Human merge gate is honored — agents may open PRs; they do not merge when policy forbids it.
- [ ] Canonical docs/skill prose lead with npm + `directive update` / `deft update` (not Go release-asset discovery as the happy path).
- [ ] `deft-directive-sync` (or successor upgrade handoff) does not treat submodule update as the primary consumer upgrade path.
- [ ] Missing global CLI / PATH problems surface actionable install remediation (`npm i -g @deftai/directive@latest`), not manual GitHub release-asset archaeology.
- [ ] Tests or skill-contract checks cover: stop-after-commit is a failure mode; terminal states are named; human-merge path does not claim `released` without merge.

## Related

- #761 / #2274 / #1409 / #2064 — npm + `directive update` / `doctor` as canonical upgrade (closed; deposit path)
- #1598 — build skill should finish with explicit commit/PR handoff (same handoff class)
- #2849 — transactional dirty-worktree checkpoints (possible `blocked` input)
- #1193 — human merge / intent ceiling
- #1158 — upgrade docs cited unexposed task aliases (**closed** as superseded by CLI-first recovery)
- #803 — schema pin/cadence docs (**closed** as superseded by in-repo xBRIEF 0.8 + UPGRADING)

## Context

Filed from a consumer update session (2026-06-12). Body rewritten 2026-08-03 to match current npm-first install stack while preserving the original operator-goal gap (deposit ≠ released on default branch).

narratives.UserStory: As a consumer operator upgrading Directive, I want the upgrade workflow to carry a successful deposit through SCM release handoff, so that the session ends in an explicit terminal state (released, pr-open, or blocked) rather than a silent stop after a local framework-only commit.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. Audit deft-directive-sync and related upgrade/docs prose for stop-after-local-commit and submodule-first paths; inventory terminal-state gaps against issue #1604 AC. 2. Define and implement upgrade handoff terminal states (released | pr-open | blocked:<reason>) in skill/docs guidance after successful deposit. 3. Wire policy detection (allowDirectCommitsToMaster / requireHumanMerge / branch protection) into PR-oriented vs direct-commit paths without auto-merge past the human merge gate. 4. Lead canonical upgrade prose with npm + directive/deft update + doctor; demote submodule/Go installer to legacy/back-compat. 5. Surface missing-CLI remediation as npm i -g @deftai/directive@latest. 6. Add skill-contract or unit checks that treat silent stop-after-commit as a failure mode and assert named terminal states. 7. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry; run pre-pr + full task check before PR.
